name: Mattermost bridge for Matrix
description: This plugin provides a bridge connecting Mattermost and Matrix servers.

settings.help_text: Health of the bridge, what is bridged to what and what is waiting. Check again after changing a setting.
Client-Server API URL of the Matrix homeserver as reachable from the Mattermost server (e.g. https://matrix.example.com or http://synapse:8008).
Application Service token for creating ghost users (required for proper user attribution). Copy this token to your Matrix homeserver registration file as 'as_token'.
settings.regenerate_help_text: Generate a new secure token (remember to update your Matrix homeserver registration file)

settings.help_text: Homeserver token for Matrix Application Service registration. Copy this token to your Matrix homeserver registration file as 'hs_token'.
settings.regenerate_help_text: Generate a new secure token (remember to update your Matrix homeserver registration file)

settings.help_text: Bearer token for Prometheus to read /metrics. When empty, the metrics endpoint accepts the homeserver token instead, which gives whoever configures Prometheus the credential the homeserver uses; set a separate token to avoid that.
settings.regenerate_help_text: Generate a new token (update the Prometheus scrape configuration)

settings.help_text: Enable bridging between Mattermost and Matrix. Both directions require this.

Allow direct and group messages to be bridged to private Matrix rooms. Nothing is bridged unless every person in a conversation agrees with /matrix dm on; anyone can turn it off with /matrix dm off. Matrix server administrators can read the bridged rooms.

settings.display_name: Create Channels for Invited Rooms (team name)
settings.help_text: Team name (as in the team's address). When set, a moderator of a Matrix room who invites the bridge bot gets a new public channel in this team, bridged to the room. When their Matrix account is linked, they become its admin. Empty turns this off.

Let the bridge read and write messages in end-to-end encrypted Matrix rooms. The bridge bot holds the room keys, so messages are readable by the bridge and by Mattermost. Requires org.matrix.msc3202 in the registration file (the downloadable file includes it) and the matching homeserver setting (see docs/ENCRYPTION.md).

When Bridge Encrypted Rooms is on, keep a copy of the bridge's room keys on the Matrix homeserver, encrypted with a backup key the bridge keeps sealed in Mattermost's database. If the bridge loses its encryption state, it restores the keys and can read earlier messages again. The sealed key sits next to the state it protects: to survive losing the whole database, copy the key with /matrix encryption-backup-key and put it in Encryption Backup Key below. Off by default.

Only for recovery: the backup key shown by /matrix encryption-backup-key, supplied after the bridge lost its database so it can restore its room keys from the homeserver. Leave empty otherwise. Used only when the bridge has no backup key of its own stored.

When Bridge Encrypted Rooms is on, rooms the bridge creates for direct and group messages (after everyone agreed with /matrix dm on) start with end-to-end encryption, so Matrix server administrators cannot read them. Needs the encryption device to be running; ignored otherwise. Off by default.

settings.display_name: Send Typing, Presence and Read Receipts
settings.help_text: Show who is typing, who is online and what they have read to people in Matrix. Typing events only reach channel members, so a small bot account (matrix-bridge-events) joins every bridged channel. Status and read state are checked every 30 seconds. In a cluster one server does this work.
How often status, custom status and read state are checked when typing, presence and read receipts are on. The minimum is 2.
Prefix for Mattermost accounts created for Matrix users (e.g. 'matrix' creates matrix:alice). Change only before any Matrix users have been bridged.

⚠️ ADVANCED: Takes over a DEDICATED Matrix homeserver to mirror Mattermost. Creates real Matrix accounts (@username:server-name) with synced profiles so people can log in with Element. Requires the mirror-mode user namespace in the registration file.
The homeserver's server_name, i.e. the domain part of Matrix user IDs (e.g. 'example.com' for @user:example.com). Leave empty when it equals the hostname of the Matrix Server URL.

Not recommended. When empty, mirrored Matrix accounts are created without any credentials and people claim them with /matrix claim or shared login. When set, every mirrored account gets this one password.

settings.display_name: Import bot and integration posts in /matrix history
settings.help_text: When /matrix history copies a channel's past messages, also copy what bots and integrations (CI, alerts, webhooks) posted. They arrive as the bot's own Matrix account, and webhooks that override their name keep it. Off by default.

When /matrix welcome tells someone their Matrix ID in a direct message, also send it by email. Needs Mattermost's email (SMTP) settings to work; a failed email is logged and never stops the welcome. Off by default.

When a Matrix person first writes in a bridged room, link them to the Mattermost account with the same verified email address instead of creating a separate account. Needs the Matrix Admin Access Token to read the Matrix account's verified email. Off by default.
Optional. A Synapse admin access token that lets /matrix claim set a one-time password for a mirrored account. Not needed when people sign in to Matrix with shared login.

Optional. When your homeserver delegates sign-in to Matrix Authentication Service (MAS), the address the bridge reaches MAS at, for example https://mas.example.com. Mirrored accounts are then also created in MAS so people can sign in with your identity provider. See docs/MIRROR_MODE_SETUP.md.
The client ID of a MAS client that is listed under policy.data.admin_clients and may use the client credentials grant.
The secret of that MAS client.

Optional. The ID of the upstream OpenID Connect provider in MAS that Mattermost also signs people in with. When set, a mirrored account is linked to the person's identity there, so signing in lands on it without matching names.

Audio and video are not relayed between Mattermost Calls and Matrix. Presence announces calls in both directions (who started, who is in, how to join, when it ended). Presence and Element Call additionally lets /matrix call start a call that both sides can join through the Element Call URL below.

options.display_name: Presence - announce calls on both sides [Recommended]
Presence and Element Call - calls both sides can join

settings.help_text: Where /matrix call sends people. May contain {room_id}, {room_name}, {display_name} and {user_id}, which are URL-escaped. Use the room address format of your Element Call deployment.
Used for the Join in Element button on calls that start in Matrix. When empty the link goes through matrix.to.
Freezes the set of Matrix accounts and rooms while a community moves from Mattermost to Matrix: nothing new is created, everything that exists keeps syncing.
Automatically sync display names and avatars from Mattermost to Matrix in Mirror Mode.
Controls how aggressively the bridge sends requests to your Matrix server to prevent rate limiting.

options.display_name: Disabled - No rate limiting (maximum performance, risk of 429 errors)
Relaxed - Light throttling (fast, suitable for dedicated Matrix servers)
Automatic - Balanced throttling (good performance with safety) [Recommended]
Conservative - Heavy throttling (safest, matches Synapse defaults exactly)
Restricted - Maximum throttling (slowest, for shared/limited Matrix servers)

settings.help_text:
Download the registration file for your Matrix homeserver.
 
**Setup Instructions:**
1. Save the settings on this page, then download the file using the button above
2. Copy it to your Matrix homeserver (e.g. /data/mattermost-bridge-registration.yaml)
3. Add the file path to homeserver.yaml under 'app_service_config_files'
4. Restart your Matrix homeserver and run /matrix test in any channel

See the [Matrix Application Service spec](https://spec.matrix.org/v1.14/application-service-api/) for details.
